question: Should ClawHub adopt this durable catalog-distribution state as the internal prerequisite for the signed feed protocol proposed in the RFC and the open transport follow-up?
rationale: The patch is intentionally a new persistent protocol layer with no current public endpoint, so correctness alone cannot determine whether its data-retention and contract boundary should become the repository’s supported foundation.

options.title: Sponsor the state foundation
options.body: Approve the durable-state boundary after live Convex proof, then review the signed transport as a separate follow-up.

options.title: Narrow or redesign the contract
options.body: Request changes to the revision, retention, or schema-export contract before accepting persistent state that later feed routes will depend on.

options.title: Defer the feed program
options.body: Pause this draft until the RFC and product ownership establish a supported catalog-feed direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the state foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the durable-state boundary after live Convex proof, then review the signed transport as a separate follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available adjacent routing candidate for publisher/catalog state, although current-main ownership evidence is limited.
